A_target.statement:
Let $k$ be a [[Definition:Field (Abstract Algebra)|field]] and $V \subseteq k^n$ an [[Definition:Affine Variety|affine variety]].
Then the [[Definition:Ring (Abstract Algebra)|ring]] of [[Definition:Polynomial Function|polynomial functions]] on $V$ is:
:$\map k V \cong k \sqbrk {x_1, \ldots, x_n} / \map I V$
where $\map I V$ is the [[Definition:Ideal of Ring|ideal]] of polynomials vanishing on $V$.

B_source.statement:
Let $S \subseteq X$ and let $R$ be a [[Definition:Ring (Abstract Algebra)|ring]] of functions on $X$.
Then restriction to $S$ is a [[Definition:Ring Homomorphism|ring homomorphism]] whose [[Definition:Kernel of Ring Homomorphism|kernel]] is the ideal of functions vanishing on $S$.

substitutions.the ambient ring of functions: the polynomial ring in n variables
substitutions.the functions vanishing on the subset: the vanishing ideal of the variety
substitutions.the ring of functions on the subset: the coordinate ring of the variety

derived.restriction is surjective onto functions: every polynomial function on V extends to the ambient space by construction
derived.the collapse by the vanishing ideal: two polynomials agree on V exactly when their difference lies in the vanishing ideal

object_map.reformulation: Present functions on a subvariety as ambient functions collapsed by those that cannot be distinguished on it.

validity_conditions: Restriction of polynomials to V is a ring homomorphism whose image is by definition the polynomial functions on V, so it is surjective onto its target.
Its kernel is exactly the set of polynomials vanishing at every point of V, which is the vanishing ideal.
The vanishing ideal is radical, so the coordinate ring is reduced; without that observation the quotient could carry nilpotents not detected by any function value.
proof_plan: Restriction $\rho: k \sqbrk {x_1, \ldots, x_n} \to \map k V$, $\map \rho f = f \restriction_V$, is a [[Definition:Surjection|surjective]] [[Definition:Ring Homomorphism|ring homomorphism]] by definition of $\map k V$.

We have:
:$\map \ker \rho = \set {f: \forall p \in V: \map f p = 0} = \map I V$

By the [[First Isomorphism Theorem for Rings]]:
:$k \sqbrk {x_1, \ldots, x_n} / \map I V \cong \map k V$
